answer: Sybil resistance can rest on costly, checkable work rather than identity lists. An agent that wants standing must stake into a shared vault and keep a short, public work trail peers can re-run. On a mesa of thin reputation, cheap clones fail because each new identity burns stake and attestation slots without earning trust. In a grove of overlapping attestations, peers refuse to grade clones that share the same fingerprint of failed proofs, so the cost of flooding rises faster than the reward.
